transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump, China's Xi Jinping, Russia's Vladimir Putin, will soon sit down for talks.
And here's Jennifer Pack has more on how recent revelations that Nvidia's then CEO, Jensen
Wang, was having an affair with alleged Chinese spy could affect the summit.
This Nvidia case has brought to the surface allegations of China trying to smuggle high-end
U.S. chips, bypassing a U.S. ban, and of allegations of Chinese espionage.
Beijing, by the way, has denied the Nvidia spy allegation.
But this week, the Commerce Department has further restricted China's access to high-end
chips.
That could be a big hit to Chinese AI firms, which are doing cutting-edge work.
Whereas the Chinese Foreign -- Chinese Commerce Ministry and the Foreign Ministry, they've
both condemned this, saying the U.S. is abusing export controls and overreaching with its
concept of national security threats.
NPR's Jennifer Pack reporting.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth signed a military agreement with Venezuela today.
NPR's Kerry Kahn reports it's the latest Trump administration official to visit since capturing
then-President Nicolas Maduro last January.
Hegseth told a gathering of U.S. and Venezuelan officials that the deal re-establishes military
ties and will involve joint training and intelligence sharing.
Details of the deal were not made public.
Hegseth says close cooperation with interim President Delci Rodriguez has stabilized Venezuela
and "ridded of narco-terrorists once and for all."
The U.S. has killed at least 240 people off South American waters, claiming they were
drug traffickers without providing evidence.
The Defense Secretary also praised a recent oil deal that gives the U.S. control over
some Venezuelan oil reserves.
Details of that deal are also not public.
Kerry Kahn, NPR News, Rio de Janeiro.
Democrats knew congressional majorities could mean some big education changes on the horizon,
including student loans, as NPR's Corey Turner reports.
Speaking on Wednesday, Senator Bernie Sanders said federal student loan policy is "an absolute
priority" for him once Democrats retake control of Congress.
Specifically, he's pushing back on the strict new loan limits Republicans created for many
professional training programs, including in nursing and other healthcare-related jobs.
The idea that the Trump administration has provided disincentives for people to get into
professions that we desperately need through their student loan policy is absurd.
In the next Congress, Sanders is expected to lead the Senate committee that handles
education.
Corey Turner, NPR News.
Enthropic has priced its initial public offering at $83 per share ahead of its debut on Wall
Street tomorrow.
It's above the expected price range and values the maker of clawed AI at $1.5 trillion.
It comes at a moment when investors are nervous of an AI boom overly reliant on debt.
This is NPR.
The top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee is beginning to lay the groundwork for long-promised
investigations of the Trump administration.
California Congressman Robert Garcia has sent letters directing members of President Trump's
family and top administration officials to preserve documents.
Investigations include alleged financial conflicts involving Trump's family, administration's
handling of files related to Jeffrey Epstein.
Grand Theft Auto VI comes out at midnight tonight.
NPR's James Mastromorino reports its busting records, not just for the video game industry.
It's even eclipsing the biggest movie openings.
Grand Theft Auto VI is the first game in the controversial crime series in 13 years.
Millions of players across the world are already digging into it.
The game's estimated to have cost a billion dollars to make, and that investment already
seems to be paying off.
GTA VI is on track to make over $2 billion within hours of its worldwide launch.
It's more money than the opening weekends of blockbuster movies, Spider-Man brand-new-day,
and Avengers Endgame combined.
Eager fans are calling off work to play the game in productivity losses that could measurably
dent the U.S. economy before smoothing out in the coming months.
James Mastromorino, NPR News.
Saint Peter's Basilica is marking the 400th anniversary of its dedication.
Its construction spanned 120 years, enduring the Protestant Reformation and the sack of
Rome in the 16th century.
It was built over what was said to be the burial site of the Apostle Peter.
I'm Rylan Barton.
This is NPR News from Washington.
This message comes from VCU.
At Virginia Commonwealth University, research is knowledge put to work.
Ranked among the nation's top 50 public research universities, VCU is expanding what's known
and what's possible.
